reference:
To identify who Neleus of Scepsis studied under in addition to Theophrastus, we examine the paragraph about Neleus of Scepsis: "Neleus of Scepsis ( ; Greek: Νηλεύς ), was the son of Coriscus of Scepsis. He was a disciple of Aristotle and Theophrastus, the latter of whom bequeathed to him his library, and appointed him one of his executors."

From this, we find that Neleus of Scepsis studied under Aristotle in addition to Theophrastus.

FINDING: Neleus of Scepsis studied under Aristotle in addition to Theophrastus.

Hop 2: Examine the paragraphs for other philosophers in the Peripatetic school during the same period as Neleus of Scepsis.

The paragraphs mention Phaenias of Eresus and Lyco of Troas as part of the Peripatetic school during the time Neleus of Scepsis was studying. Phaenias of Eresus joined Theophrastus in the Peripatetic school, and Lyco of Troas succeeded Strato as the head of the school, indicating they were contemporaries with Neleus.

FINDING: Phaenias of Eresus and Lyco of Troas were contemporaries of Neleus of Scepsis in the Peripatetic school.
